messages:
ashley: Heads-up: DEN pop p99 shot up to ~1.8s around 03:20 UTC, throughput dropped ~30%. Dashboard: https://redwood.metrics/den-pop/latency . Any recent rollouts or infra changes?

maria: Not aware of any app rollouts. No config pushes in the last 24h for DEN. Seeing same on synthetic canaries.

kevin: I can repro on a few traces — kernels are flipping between latency and throughput picks frequently. Looks like kernel-selector oscillation.

leo: @kevin can you paste the selector logs? We had a subtle change to the heuristic last week.

kevin: selector logs (tail):
```
2026-03-18T03:18:02Z kernel_selector: pick=latency_opt, score=0.72
2026-03-18T03:18:03Z kernel_selector: pick=throughput_opt, score=0.69
2026-03-18T03:18:05Z kernel_selector: pick=latency_opt, score=0.71
2026-03-18T03:18:06Z kernel_selector: pick=throughput_opt, score=0.68
```
Oscillation every ~1-2s.

ashley: That jives with the p99 spikes — context switch patterns jump when kernels flip. Any KV cache behaviour change?

kevin: KV cache hit-rate dipped from 98% -> 87% at same time window. Maybe eviction churn from batching change?

maria: Running a quick flame/prof snapshot on a sample host now.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Rollout "batching-heuristic-v2" completed in denver-pop at 2026-03-18T02:50:10Z by infra-team.

ashley: Hmm, batching-heuristic-v2 rollout completed 30m before incident. Could be related.

leo: net-eng: are there any peering / path changes recorded for DEN around 03:15-03:30?

net-eng: We saw an upstream IX peer re-advertise a path to a transit at 03:19 UTC. BGP AS path changed for some prefixes. Provider says an intermediate AS did a soft-reconfig.

maria: Profiler shows a big increase in recv latency inside runtime around same time, and syscalls per request go up ~25% — suggests networking jitter.

kevin: So two hypotheses: (A) network path jitter causing more RPC latencies which trick kernel-selector into switching to throughput kernel, which then increases batch handling latency and evicts KV cache more, or (B) batching heuristic rollout increased sensitivity and amplified the noisy network signal.

ashley: I can flip the kernel-selector to prefer latency_opt for DEN as a temporary mitigation. Any objections?

leo: +1 do it. Also suggest we pin batching heuristic back to previous version on DEN while we investigate.

ashley: Doing kernel-pin now: sudo /opt/redwood/runtime/bin/ksel --pin latency_opt --scope pop:denver

sre-bot: action: kernel-pin applied to denver-pop by ashley at 2026-03-18T03:40:12Z.

kevin: After pin: p50 ~30ms lower, p99 dropped to ~250ms from 1.8s, throughput recovered ~20%. KV cache hit-rate climbing back to ~96%.

maria: Flame snapshot post-pin shows syscall jitter subsiding, fewer context switches. Good short-term outcome.

ashley: Rolling back batching-heuristic-v2 on DEN (partial rollback): infra runbook -> rollback denver-pop batching-heuristic to v1

ops-bot: action: rollback initiated for batching-heuristic in denver-pop by ashley.

net-eng: Provider has opened a ticket with upstream AS, they claim config churn but no packet loss reported. We'll keep monitoring.

kevin: Logged a perf-regression ticket: PERF-6721 referencing batching-heuristic-v2 sensitivity to transient RTT variance. Adding traces and selector logs.

leo: Suggest changes: (1) add hysteresis to kernel-selector (min dwell time 10s), (2) make batching heuristic use EWMA of RTT instead of instant; (3) KV cache eviction grace when kernel change occurs.

maria: I'll attach profiler artifacts and a short repro harness to PERF-6721.

ashley: Monitoring: p99 now stable ~230-300ms for last 20m. Will keep kernel pinned until we have a patch.

kevin: Quick mitigation note for runbook: if you see p99 > 1s in a POP and selector oscillation in logs, pin latency kernel + rollback batching-heuristic to v1, then notify net-eng.

leo: Filing followups: infra will revert sensitivity, runtime team will implement selector hysteresis, network team will chase upstream config.

net-eng: FYI provider reports they made a config diff rollback at 04:05 UTC which reduced path churn. No packet loss at AS, but route flap dampening was involved.

ashley: Thanks everyone. I'll keep the thread updated if anything else crops up. :thumbsup:

ashley: postmortem TODOs: add synthetic test for selector oscillation, update runbook, backport kernel-fix and batching-hysteresis to stable.

kevin: Adding labels: incident, perf, denver, kernel-selector, batching, kvcache.

maria: saved artifacts -> s3://redwood-artifacts/incidents/1977778888/ (profiles, traces, selector-logs).

leo: Closing loop: set meeting tomorrow to triage PERF-6721 and schedule patch.
